name: Fiji
description: Fiji offers expats a tropical island lifestyle with stunning natural beauty and a relaxed pace of life. It appeals to retirees, remote workers, and those seeking a community-driven environment away from major global hubs. The cost of living is moderate compared to Western standards, and English is an official language, easing communication.
longdescription: Life as an expat in Fiji is characterized by its tropical climate, vibrant culture, and a significantly slower pace, often referred to as 'Fiji time.' The economy is largely driven by tourism, sugar exports, and remittances, offering some employment opportunities, particularly in hospitality and services. The population is diverse, blending indigenous Fijians (iTaukei) with Indo-Fijians and other ethnic groups, creating a rich cultural tapestry. Expats can expect to engage in traditional ceremonies, enjoy fresh seafood and local produce, and adapt to a communal culture of sharing. While major cities like Suva and Nadi offer more amenities and infrastructure, outer islands provide a more secluded, nature-focused experience with limited services. Safety is generally good, especially in tourist areas, but petty crime exists in urban centers, and natural disasters like cyclones are a consideration during the wet season. Healthcare facilities are concentrated in urban areas, with serious medical cases often requiring evacuation to Australia or New Zealand.

visas.name: Fiji Long-Stay Permit
visas.description: Fiji's long-stay permit allows retirees and investors to reside in Fiji for extended periods. Ideal for those seeking a peaceful Pacific island lifestyle.
benefits: Peaceful island lifestyle
330 islands to explore
English-speaking
Warm tropical climate
World-class diving and snorkeling

Proof of funds or income
Medical certificate
Police clearance
Passport photos

visas.name: Work Permit - Long Term
visas.description: The Fiji 'Work Permit - Long Term' program allows non-citizens to reside and work in Fiji for an extended period, typically up to three years. It is designed for skilled workers, professionals, technical staff, and executives whose expertise is needed by a Fijian employer and cannot be readily filled by a local citizen. This permit facilitates lawful employment and provides a pathway for long-term stay in Fiji.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are foreign nationals with a confirmed job offer from a legally registered Fijian employer, possessing qualifications and experience appropriate to the role, and meeting health and character requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Foreign nationals working in Fiji under a valid Work Permit may remain for extended periods through successive renewals. Where employment continues, and the individual maintains full immigration compliance, this pathway can establish the residency history required for long-term status, and potentially lead to permanent residence and citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The employment relationship must continue, the employer must maintain full immigration compliance, and for 'Time Post' permits, it must be demonstrated that the position cannot yet be localized. An FIRCA Tax Compliance Certificate is also required.
benefits: Legal permission to work in Fiji for an approved employer and role.
Lawful stay tied to employment, allowing residence in Fiji.
Ability to include eligible dependents (spouse and children under 18) on the same application.
Opportunity for permit renewal and extension if employment continues and conditions are met.
Establishes a lawful record of residence which can contribute towards future long-term residency options.
required_documents: Completed and signed Work Permit application form.
Valid passport (copy of bio-data page, valid for the full duration of proposed employment).
Two (2) passport-size photographs (less than 6 months old, good quality color, full-face view, plain/light background).
Employment contract or formal offer letter (clearly stating job title, duties, salary, employment terms, and duration).
Academic and professional certificates (certified copies).
Curriculum Vitae (CV) with detailed work experience and education.
Medical examination report.
Police Report from the country of citizenship (and from Fiji for renewals).
Request letter from the employer (including company profile, position description, roles, special requirements, and justification for needing a foreign national).
Employer business registration and operating license.
Evidence of local recruitment efforts (e.g., job advertisements, interview records, recruitment reports, analysis of local applications), unless exempt.
Notarized English translations for any documents not in English.
FIRCA Tax Compliance Certificate (for renewals).
Training Program details and local understudy information (especially for 'Time Post' permits).
application_process_steps: The sponsoring employer finalizes the job offer and gathers all necessary company registration and tax documents.
The applicant compiles all required personal documents, including passport, CV, qualifications, police clearances, and medical reports.
The employer completes the work permit application forms, attaching all supporting documentation, including evidence of local recruitment efforts.
The employer submits the complete application package to the Fiji Immigration Department and pays the applicable fees.
The Immigration Department assesses the application, and if approved, issues the work permit.
Upon approval, the foreign national receives entry clearance, travels to Fiji, and commences employment.

visas.name: Work Permit - Short Term
visas.description: The Work Permit - Short Term program in Fiji is designed for foreign nationals possessing specialized skills or expertise that is urgently required for a limited period, typically up to 12 months. It allows individuals to undertake specific project-based work, technical services, or short-term assignments in Fiji.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a skilled professional, IT contractor, event management specialist, or consultant with a confirmed job offer from a registered Fijian employer, whose expertise is needed for a temporary duration.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Short-Term Work Permit itself does not directly lead to permanent residency. However, maintaining a continuous lawful presence in Fiji through successive renewals of work permits (typically long-term permits) can contribute to meeting the residency history requirements for potential long-term residence or naturalization after a continuous period.
visas.renewal_conditions: Renewal is possible if the employment relationship continues and the employer still requires the foreign worker's services. Applications must be submitted before the current permit expires with updated supporting documentation reflecting the ongoing role and the employer's compliance record.
visas.tax_implications: Individuals holding a work permit under a contract of employment not exceeding 3 years may qualify as 'temporary residents' for tax purposes. Temporary residents are taxed only on Fiji-source income; foreign-source income and foreign capital gains are exempt from Fiji taxation for the duration of this status.
benefits: Legal authorization to work in Fiji for the approved duration.
Lawful residency tied to the employment permit.
Opportunity for eligible dependents to join the permit holder.
Potential for permit renewal or extension if employment continues.
Establishes a lawful record of residence that may aid future long-term immigration options.
required_documents: Completed and signed 'Application Work Permit' Form
Request letter from the employer on company letterhead, detailing position, duties, salary, terms, and justification for hiring a foreign worker
Police Report from the country of citizenship/residence (for any country resided in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years) for the principal applicant, and spouse/children if applicable
Medical Report (completed within 3 months of application) for the principal applicant, and spouse/children if applicable
Certified copy of applicant's passport biodata page (and for spouse/children if applicable)
Signed Terms & Conditions on the application form
Curriculum Vitae (CV) with certified copies of academic qualifications and references for proof of work experience
Company Registration documents (for the employer)
Valid FRCS Tax Compliance Certificate (for the employer)
Contract of Employment
Proof of local recruitment efforts (advertisements, responses, reasons for non-selection of local candidates), unless exempted
Return flight ticket (for permits up to one year)
Two certified passport-sized photographs
application_process_steps: The employer identifies the need for foreign expertise, defines the role, and prepares a job offer.
The employer conducts local recruitment efforts, unless exempted by policy (e.g., government contracts, intra-company secondments).
The employer and applicant gather all required personal and company documents, including police and medical reports.
The employer completes and signs the 'Application Work Permit' form and submits it, along with all supporting documents and the applicable fees, to the Fiji Immigration Department.
The Fiji Immigration Department reviews the application and may request additional information or clarification.

Upon approval, the work permit or relevant visa endorsement is issued, allowing the employee to enter Fiji (if applying from abroad) or commence work (if already in Fiji with appropriate entry authorization).

visas.name: Investor Permit (Seven-Year)
visas.description: The Fiji Investor Permit (Seven-Year) is a residency scheme designed for foreign investors who commit a significant financial investment in an approved business within the Fijian economy. This permit allows the holder and their immediate family to live and operate a business in Fiji for an initial period of seven years, serving as a pathway to potential permanent residency and citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign investor who intends to actively run an approved business in Fiji with a minimum investment of F$250,000, and who seeks long-term residency in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Time spent residing in Fiji under the Investor Permit counts towards the requirement of accumulating at least five years of cumulative residence within a ten-year period to become eligible for Fijian citizenship by naturalization. Fiji allows dual citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable provided the approved business operates and maintains compliance, including submitting regular business progress reports to the Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (Investment Fiji).
visas.tax_implications: Fiji operates a residence-based worldwide taxation model for full residents. However, individuals designated as 'temporary residents' (typically those on fixed-term employment contracts not exceeding 3 years) may be exempt from Fiji taxation on foreign-source income and foreign capital gains. Standard resident tax rules apply unless specific exemptions for the investor permit holder's circumstances are granted.
benefits: Residency rights for seven years, allowing the investor and family to live in Fiji.
Permission to work and operate an approved business within Fiji.
Pathway to permanent residency and eventual Fijian citizenship.
Opportunity to invest in a stable, tourism-driven economy with government incentives.
Dual citizenship is permitted, allowing retention of original nationality.
required_documents: Completed and signed Investor Permit Application Form (Form No: FID-005)
Two (2) recent passport size photographs (less than 6 months old, good quality colour, full-face view, plain/light background)
Request Letter from the Company
Company Profile/Background
Company Registration Certificate (from Registrar of Companies)
Fiji Revenue and Customs Service – Tax Identification Number (TIN)
Reserve Bank of Fiji letter – Stating the classification of ordinary shares per Investor/Shareholder and confirmation of issuance of shares
Certified copy of applicant's passport bio-data page
Individual Foreign Bank Statement
Foreign Company's Bank Statement (where applicable)
Investment approval letter from the Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (now Investment Fiji)
Certified copy of a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) issued by FTIB/Investment Fiji
Police reports from the applicant's country of citizenship and any country where they have lived for 12 months or more in the last 10 years
Medical reports conducted within three (3) months or less from the date of application
Certified copies of family members' passport bio-data pages (if accompanied by family)
Certified copy of marriage certificate (if married and accompanied by spouse)
Certified copy of children's birth certificates (if accompanied by children)
Detailed justification for the investment
Experience and qualifications in the proposed field of activity
Confirmed financial contribution by each stakeholder
Company's contact details (email, postal address, phone, location)
Endorsements from relevant authorities (e.g., Ministry of Agriculture, Lands, Tourism - if applicable)
Translated certified copies of all non-English documents in English (by registered translator)
application_process_steps: Confirm the business type is approved and determine the appropriate permit tier (7-year for F$250,000+ investment).
Obtain a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) from Investment Fiji.
Gather all required documents, including proof of funds, passport, police clearances, and medical reports.
Complete and sign the Investor Permit Application Form (FID-005).
Lodge the Investor Permit application with the Ministry of Immigration, either online or at an immigration office.
Set up and operate the approved business, fulfill any bond requirements, and ensure permit renewal before expiry while the business continues operation.

visas.name: Investor Permit (Three-Year)
visas.description: The Investor Permit (Three-Year) in Fiji is designed for foreign investors who are involved in a business project approved by the Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (FTIB) with a minimum investment. It allows non-citizens to reside in Fiji and actively operate their approved business.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign investor aged 18 or over, seeking to establish and actively run a business in Fiji with a minimum investment of F$50,000 in an approved project.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Investor Permit provides a pathway to permanent residency. To apply for Fiji citizenship, an applicant must have lived in Fiji for a total of five years within the last ten years.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable as long as the investment is maintained and the approved business remains operational. Renewal requires submitting an extension application form along with updated documentation.
benefits: Opportunity to live and work in Fiji by operating an approved business.
Pathway to permanent residency after meeting specific residence requirements.
Allows for the inclusion of dependants (spouse and children).
Fiji offers strategic location and business opportunities in sectors like tourism, agriculture, and real estate.
required_documents: Completed and signed Investor Permit Application Form (Form No: FID-005)
Investment approval letter from Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (FTIB) detailing shareholding structure
Certified copy of a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) from FTIB
Certified copies of the applicant's passport (bio-data page)
Police reports from the applicant's country of citizenship and any country where they have lived for 12 months or more in the last 10 years
Medical reports dated within three months of the application
Two recent passport-size photographs
Company Profile/Background
Company Registration Certificate
Fiji Revenue and Customs Services – Tax Identification Number (TIN)
Reserve Bank of Fiji letter – stating the classification of ordinary shares per Investor/Shareholder
Individual Foreign Bank Statement
Foreign Company's Bank Statement (where applicable)
Certified copy of Birth Certificate for all Dependents (if applicable)
Certified copy of Marriage Certificate for Spouse (if applicable)
Copy of COVID-19 Vaccination Card (for applicant and all dependents)
application_process_steps: Obtain an Investment Approval Letter and a Foreign Investment Certificate from the Fiji Trade and Investment Bureau (FTIB) for a business project with a minimum investment of F$50,000.
Complete and sign the Investor Permit Application Form (Form No: FID-005).
Gather all required supporting documents, including passport copies, police reports, medical reports, company registration documents, bank statements, and photographs.
Submit the completed application form and all supporting documents to the Department of Immigration.
Pay the requisite processing fee (amount not specified in public sources).
Await the decision on the application; processing typically takes around 21 working days after the investment certificate is in place.

visas.name: Co-extensive Permit (Dependents of Student Permit Holders)
visas.description: The Co-extensive Permit in Fiji allows the spouse and dependent children of an international student holding a valid Student Permit to reside in Fiji. This permit enables family members to live with the principal student during their period of study.
visas.target_applicant: Spouses and dependent children (generally under 21 years old) of individuals who have been granted a Student Permit to study at a recognized educational institution in Fiji.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable and its validity does not exceed the duration of the principal student permit holder's permit. Renewal applications should be lodged one (1) month prior to the expiry date of the permit.
benefits: Allows the dependent to legally reside in Fiji with the student permit holder.
Provides legal status for family unity during the student's studies.
Permit validity is linked to the principal student's permit duration, allowing for stays concurrent with the study program.
required_documents: Completed and signed application form for Co-extensive Residence Permit - Family Member
Two (2) recent passport photos of the applicant
Request letter from the Principal Applicant (student permit holder)
Certified copy of the dependent applicant's passport bio-data page
Certified copy of the dependent applicant's current arrival stamp / permit stamp (if already in Fiji)
Principal Applicant's copy of valid passport bio-data & permit
Bank statement or Scholarship Award Letter (proof of financial means from the principal student)
Police Report (valid for 1 year from date of issue) from countries of citizenship/residency if lived there for 12 months or more in the last 10 years
Medical Report (less than 3 months old from date of issue)
Certified copy of birth certificate (for dependent children)
Certified copy of marriage certificate (for spouse)
Bond (if required, details to be confirmed on payment)
Confirmed return airline ticket or ship ticket (if bond is not paid)
application_process_steps: Obtain and complete the 'Application Form for Co-extensive Residence Permit - Family Member'.
Gather all required supporting documentation, including passport photos, certified copies of passports, financial proof from the principal student, police reports, and medical reports.
Submit the complete application form and documents to the Fiji Department of Immigration.
Pay the applicable application fee upon submission or when the permit is approved (a bond may also be required).
Await a decision from the Department of Immigration. Processing times may vary depending on completeness and verification needs.

visas.name: Exemption Status for Child of a Fiji Citizen
visas.description: This status is for foreign citizens who are direct descendants (children, grandchildren, or great-grandchildren) of an individual who held Fiji citizenship on October 10, 1970. It grants the holder the right to enter, reside, study, and work in Fiji without the need for a separate permit.
visas.target_applicant: A foreign citizen holding a valid foreign passport who is a direct descendant of a person who was a citizen of Fiji on October 10, 1970.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Exemption status holders can reside and work in Fiji for up to 3 years, which contributes to the general residency requirement for naturalization (typically 5 years out of 10).
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain eligibility, adhere to the laws of Fiji, and not engage in conduct prejudicial to the peace, order, good government, or morale of the people of Fiji. Failure to comply may result in cancellation.
benefits: Ability to enter Fiji without a permit.
Right to reside in Fiji.
Permission to study in Fiji.
Authorization to work in Fiji without a work permit.
Exemption from lodgment fees.
required_documents: Request Letter from the applicant (or parent if under 18).
Support Letter from the applicant's guardian and copy of guardian's valid national photo ID (if under 18 and not residing with parents in Fiji).
Certified copy of the applicant's passport bio-data page.
One recent passport size photo.
Certified copy of Birth Certificate.
Copy of parents' passport bio-data pages (if applicant is below 18 years of age).
Certified copy of Marriage Certificate (if applicable).
Copy of Foreign Citizenship Certificate (if applicable).
Police Report from country of citizenship or current residence (if applicant is above 18 years of age).
Medical Report.
Official documents to prove the past or present existence of the principal citizen (e.g., Fiji passport, Fiji Citizenship Certificate, Birth Certificate, Death Certificate, Marriage Certificate).
Official documents to prove the applicant's familial relationship to the principal citizen (e.g., relevant Birth Certificates, Marriage Certificates, Death Certificates).
application_process_steps: Complete the approved online application form.
Gather all required official records and information to establish eligibility.
Submit the application with all supporting documents.
Receive an exemption approval letter upon successful application.

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Long-stay permit available for retirees and investors
- Temporary residence for those with Fijian family connections
- Investment visa for property buyers and business investors

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Children born outside Fiji on or after April 10, 2009, are eligible for citizenship by registration if either parent was a Fijian citizen at the time of birth. Children born to a Fijian parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent can also register for citizenship by descent through a Fijian mission abroad.

Naturalization.desc: A foreign national can apply for Fiji citizenship by naturalization. From the commencement of the Citizenship of Fiji (Amendment) Act 2026 until January 1, 2035, applicants must have lawfully lived in Fiji for a total of eight years within the ten years immediately before applying. After January 1, 2035, applicants must also hold a valid permanent residence permit in addition to the eight-year residency requirement. Applicants must be of good character, intend to continue residing in Fiji, and have adequate knowledge of the English language and duties/privileges of citizenship. Naturalization applications were suspended from October 2025 pending the 2026 reforms.

Birthright.desc: Any person born in Fiji on or after April 10, 2009, automatically receives citizenship at birth, unless one parent has diplomatic immunity and neither parent is a citizen. Individuals born between 1990 and 1997 only received citizenship if at least one parent was a Fijian citizen.

Spouse and Family.desc: Foreign spouses of Fijian citizens can apply for naturalization. Under the Citizenship of Fiji Decree 2009, applicants must have been lawfully present in Fiji for a total of three of the five years immediately before the application. However, under the 2026 amendments, permanent residence is becoming a required stepping-stone for spouses from 2030.

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax:** Progressive rates from 0% to 20%. The first FJD 30,000 is tax-free, income between FJD 30,001 and FJD 50,000 is taxed at 18%, and income above FJD 50,000 is taxed at 20%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed on local income only.
- **Corporate Tax:** Standard rate of 20%.
- **Value Added Tax (VAT):** Reduced to 12.5% effective from August 1, 2025.
- **Capital Gains Tax:** There is no capital gains tax in Fiji.
- **Wealth Tax:** None.
- **Non-resident Withholding Tax:** On insurance premiums, increased to 3.75% to align with the corporate tax rate.
- **Tax Incentives:** Various incentives are available for foreign investors, particularly for export growth, employment generation, housing, and certain tour activities, including a 25% investment allowance for non-accommodation tour activities. Expanded tax deductions for certain business donations and employment also apply.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** A single person can expect estimated monthly costs of around FJ$3,205 (approximately £1,121 or $908 USD) excluding rent, while a family of four might spend around FJ$6,026 (approximately £1,651 or $2,129.7 USD) excluding rent. Rent for a one-bedroom apartment in a city center averages £604 (USD 603.60) per month. Imported goods can be expensive due to transport costs.
- **Language:** English is an official language and widely spoken in government, education, and business. Learning basic Fijian phrases like 'bula' (hello) and 'vinaka' (thank you) is appreciated. Fiji Hindi is also spoken by the Indo-Fijian community.
- **Safety:** Fiji is generally safe, especially in resort areas and outer islands. However, petty crime such as pickpocketing and bag snatching can occur in urban areas like Suva and Nadi, particularly in crowded markets and transport centers. Avoid walking alone at night in unlit or uncrowded places.
- **Registration:** A visitor permit is typically issued on arrival for up to 4 months, extendable to 6 months. For longer stays, an investor/retiree permit is available for those aged 45+ with a minimum income of $1,500/month. Work permits require a job offer and employer application through the Fiji Department of Immigration.
- **Healthcare:** Public healthcare is accessible but varies in quality. Many expats opt for private health insurance to access better-equipped private facilities, mainly located in Suva and Nadi. Serious medical conditions often necessitate evacuation to Australia or New Zealand.
- **Driving:** Drive cautiously as roads can be narrow, poorly lit, and shared with pedestrians and animals. Potholes and oversized speed bumps are common, and local driving habits may differ.
